posts.caption:
One small thing to do at the table today: pick a family code word.

Scammers call grandparents pretending to be a grandchild in trouble. There’s been an accident or an arrest, they need bail money today, and “please don’t tell Mom”. Some now use AI to copy a relative’s voice from a short video posted online. The FBI suggests a secret word or phrase that only your family knows.

If a call like this comes: ask for the word. Or hang up and call your grandchild on the number you already have. A real grandchild won’t mind.

Swipe for how the call usually goes (an example we wrote, based on FBI and FTC warnings).

Has your family had a call like this? Tell us at scamdb.dev/report (link in bio). Reports stay private.

Happy Thanksgiving. Share this with the family group chat.

#scamawareness #elderfraud #fraudprevention #scamalert

posts.caption:
Black Friday is the fake shop’s favourite day.

scamdb has the same fake-shop script documented in 28 countries, from Canada to Taiwan: a famous brand at 80% off, a countdown timer, “closing down, everything must go”. The words change from country to country. The script doesn’t.

Before you pay on a site you’ve never used:
1. Know the normal price. A huge discount on a brand is the bait.
2. Search the shop’s name plus “reviews” on another site.
3. Pay by credit card. It has the most protection.
4. Paid and nothing came? Call your card issuer. It’s not your fault.

Seen a deal that looks too good? Send us the ad or message at scamdb.dev/report (link in bio). Reports stay private.

Happy (careful) shopping.

#blackfriday #scamalert #onlineshopping #fraudprevention

posts.caption:
Shopped today? Expect this text: “Did you attempt a payment of $5,000? Reply YES or NO.”

You reply no. Then a helpful “fraud specialist” calls and asks for a code, or to move your money somewhere safe. Your bank never asks you to move money to protect it. Ever. Hang up and call the number on your card.

The texts in the video are real, as published by the FBI (Apr 14, 2022).
Got one? Send it to scamdb.dev/report (link in bio). Reports stay private.
Voice: AI, made from my own.

Share this with whoever did the shopping today.

#blackfriday #scamalert #bankfraud #fraudprevention
